career_desc: Hi, I'm a front-end developer with about 6 years of experience, specializing in JavaScript, TypeScript, and ReactJS. My journey in the tech industry has allowed me to work on several impactful company projects, where I've not only honed my front-end skills but also gained valuable insights into backend development with Java Spring Boot. While front-end development is my primary focus, I bring a well-rounded approach to my work, ensuring that my projects are robust and integrated seamlessly with backend systems. Currently, I am actively broadening my technical scope by diving deeper into server-side architecture and database management to transition into a versatile Full-stack Developer. This evolution allows me to take full ownership of the development lifecycle, from crafting intuitive user interfaces to architecting scalable microservices. By merging my extensive frontend expertise with a growing mastery of the backend, I aim to build comprehensive, end-to-end solutions that drive real business value.

overview.title: J2N Project
overview.desc: J2N Projects is a full-stack project designed with a micro-frontend architecture using Turborepo for modular UI development. The backend is structured as a microservices ecosystem to ensure scalability and service isolation, with MySQL serving as the primary database for data storage and management.

frontend.title: Frontend Layer
frontend.subtitle: (Micro Frontends using Next.js)
frontend.desc: The UI layer is split into multiple independent Next.js applications, where each app is responsible for a specific business domain:

list.1: Failures in one module do not affect the others.
list.2: All frontends communicate with backend exclusively through the BFF Service, ensuring consistent data shape and shielding the UI from backend complexity.

backend.title: Backend Layer
backend.subtitle: (Microservices using Java Spring Boot)
backend.desc: The backend consists of two main parts: the BFF, the API Gateway, and a set of domain-driven microservices.

bff.title: (a) BFF Service (Backend for Frontend)
bff.desc: The BFF contains no business logic; it mainly forwards requests to the API Gateway.

list.0: Acts as an adapter between all frontend apps and the internal backend system.

sublist.2: Aggregate data from multiple services (future support)
sublist.3: Prevent FE from calling internal services directly

gateway.title: (b) API Gateway Service
gateway.desc: The API Gateway is the single controlled entry point to the backend.

list.1: Route requests to the correct micro-service
list.3: Hide internal micro-services from the client

microservices.title: (c) Microservices Layer (Java Spring Boot)
microservices.desc: Each service is a standalone Spring Boot application following the “one service, one domain” approach:

database.title: Database Layer
database.subtitle: (MySQL per Service)
database.desc: Each microservice has its own dedicated MySQL database.

list.1: Each service manages its own schema (clean domain boundaries)
list.2: Easy to migrate or scale only the services that need it
list.3: System stability is improved (failures in one DB do not affect others)

message.title: Message Layer
message.subtitle: (RabbitMQ)
message.desc: RabbitMQ is used for asynchronous communication between services.
message.desc_bottom: Each type of event has its own queue to maintain isolation and reliability.

flow.title: Request Flow & Event Flow

list.0: Frontend sends a request to the BFF Service.
list.1: BFF normalizes and forwards the request to the API Gateway.

sublist.1: Routes the request to the appropriate microservice

list.3: Microservice processes business logic and interacts with its MySQL database.
list.4: Response returns through the same chain: Service → Gateway → BFF → Frontend

list.0: A microservice triggers an event (e.g., user created, new order, image uploaded).
list.1: The service publishes the event to a specific RabbitMQ queue.
list.2: Other subscribed services receive and process the event.
list.3: Tasks run in the background without delaying the user-facing response.

flow.desc: This ensures smoother performance and better scalability.

list.0: User logs in from the frontend → BFF → Auth Service.
list.1: Auth Service returns a JWT token.
list.3: All future requests include this token through BFF → Gateway.

list.0: Single point responsible for token verification.
list.1: Internal services never receive unauthenticated direct requests.
list.2: Optional IP whitelisting for service-to-service communication.

list.0: Each service accesses only its own database.
list.1: Prevents cross-service data leakage or accidental coupling.

list.0: Only authorized services may publish or consume events.
